question: Who was appointed as the governor of Bengal by Sultan Balban after the revolt and subsequent death of Tughril Beg?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bughra Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bughra Khan, also known as Nasiruddin Bughra Khan, was the son of Sultan Balban and was appointed as the governor of Bengal after the revolt and death of Tughril Beg.
 
• Sultan Balban personally led a military campaign to suppress the rebellion of Tughril Beg in Bengal.
 
• After successfully quelling the rebellion, Balban appointed his son Bughra Khan as the governor of Bengal to ensure stability and loyalty in the region.
 
• Bughra Khan later declared his independence in Bengal, establishing a semi-autonomous rule, but maintained a nominal allegiance to the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• His appointment marked a strategic move by Balban to maintain centralized control over distant provinces while entrusting governance to trusted family members.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sultan Balban:**

 
 
• Balban was one of the most prominent rulers of the Slave Dynasty (Delhi Sultanate) and reigned from 1266 to 1287.
 
• He is known for implementing a strong centralized administration and introducing policies to curb the power of nobles and maintain royal authority.
 
 
 
• **Tughril Beg's Rebellion:**
 
 
• Tughril Beg was a rebellious governor of Bengal who declared independence from the Delhi Sultanate during Balban's reign.
 
• His revolt was suppressed by Balban after a fierce military campaign.
 
 
 
• **Governance of Bengal:**
 
 
• Bengal was a strategically significant province during the Delhi Sultanate due to its economic and political importance.
 
• Governors were often appointed from among the Sultan's trusted nobles or family members to ensure loyalty and effective administration.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Bughra Khan:**
 
 
• Although initially loyal to his father, Bughra Khan later established an independent rule in Bengal.
 
• His reign in Bengal set the stage for the emergence of independent regional kingdoms in the region during later periods.
